name: Methodology: upvote and point counts in this sentiment layer are a popularity proxy observed at a date, never a measurement of quality or of popularity in general
symptom: Every quantitative claim about community sentiment in this slice carries an upvote or Hacker News point count, and the risk is that a reader treats those numbers as results. They are not. A 182-upvote one-line reply on a 103-upvote post is not 'the community prefers X by a factor of 1.8'. Vote counts measure who has the time to write a comment that ranks, they drift after access, they are adversarially gameable, and on a subreddit like r/LocalLLaMA they are correlated with posting frequency rather than with operator experience. Hacker News points have the same property with different mechanics. Every source record in this slice carries kind: forum, status: verified only in the sense that the quoted text was read at the cited URL on the cited date.
root_cause: The fix is procedural rather than statistical. Preference claims are recorded as attributed quotes with a date and an observed vote count, the count is labelled a proxy in the record's notes, and where sentiment is divided the record states the shape of the split instead of a share. No record in this slice converts a vote count into a percentage, and no record claims a vote count is representative.
workaround: Read a vote count as 'this argument was visible to a lot of people on this date', which is a real signal about which arguments practitioners are actually arguing about. Do not use it to weight advice, and do not use this slice to make a quantitative claim about the community's beliefs. Where a practitioner states a number - five concurrent users, four users, twelve patches - that number is recorded as their statement with the caveat that it is a rule of thumb, not a measurement this repo has verified.
notes: This is the record that makes the rest of the slice honest, and the one most likely to be needed by a future slice. Two places where it already changed what was written: the Strix Halo split records the shape rather than a share, and the engine records record the refusal of a ranking as the finding rather than inventing a ranked list from scattered votes. Sampling caveat stated plainly: the corpus is heavily weighted to r/LocalLLaMA, because that is where practitioner buy/sell reasoning about hardware is discussed in public. r/MachineLearning was searched and returned no hardware-buying threads in the access window; its high-scoring threads are link shares and career discussion. So 'the community' in this slice means the self-hosted-inference community, and the bias toward hobbyist-scale builds is real.
